patch.value: pm health advises pm history-repair for history_drift_missing_stream, but history-repair refuses a stream with no entries

When an item's history stream is missing, pm health reports history_drift_missing_stream with the remedy pm history-repair <id>, rewritten to pm history-repair --all when several streams drift. history-repair cannot rebuild a missing stream: the --all row fails with 'No history entries exist for <id>; nothing to repair.' and the command exits 1. Found on PR #1762 while running the advised remedies on a mixed-drift fixture (one chain mismatch, one missing stream) in tests/integration/lifecycle/history-bridge.integration.spec.ts. The remedy registry entry lives in src/core/diagnostics/remediation.ts, and the bulk rewrite lives in rewriteBulkHealthRemediation in src/sdk/governance/health.ts. The fix names a command that actually rebuilds or records the missing stream, for example a baseline-reseed step, or a restore when an item can be rebuilt from history; it must also keep the bulk rewrite from advising --all for a code that --all cannot repair.
An integration spec runs the remedy pm health names for a missing stream, per item and in bulk, and the history_drift check is ok afterwards

value.text: A second remedy-accuracy case, from CodeRabbit on PR #1762: the drift scanner reports history_drift_chain_mismatch both for a bridgeable break and for a patch that only applies on top of the unrecorded change. So when every drifted stream is a chain mismatch, pm health advises pm history-repair --all --append-only, which bridges the first kind and refuses the second with patch_does_not_replay; strict health stays unclean. The fix belongs with this item: the scanner, or the remedy selection, must tell a bridgeable chain mismatch from one that needs the rewriting repair, and the integration spec must run each advised remedy to a clean history_drift check.

value.text: Implementation on branch fix/history-remedies-converge, 2026-11-21. (1) Missing stream: history-repair, in both the rewriting and the append-only mode, rebuilds a live item's absent or record-less stream (src/sdk/history/reseed.ts). It writes one sealed history_repair baseline from the empty document to the on-disk item, after any whitespace the stream held, with context.history_reseed {contract_version 1, reason missing_stream|empty_stream, prior_versions unrecorded}, and the result carries a typed reseed receipt. runHistoryMaintenance takes an optional reseed plan, called only for a live item, so a deleted item's empty stream and the evidence-bound modes (merge reconcile audit, receipt proofs, forced audit) keep refusing. The default history.missing_stream auto_create policy recreates a deleted stream as an empty file on read, which is why the reported refusal was 'nothing to repair' rather than 'no stream'. (2) Chain mismatch, from the CodeRabbit comment: pm health now runs the append-only repair's own preview for every chain-mismatched stream (src/sdk/governance/health/history-drift-remedies.ts). A refusal turns the warning into history_drift_chain_unbridgeable with the remedy pm history-repair <id>. When the rewriting preview refuses too, the warning becomes history_drift_chain_unrepairable with the remedy pm history <id> --verify --full plus a version-control restore. details.chain_unbridgeable lists each stream with its reason and rewrite_refusal. (3) Running the remedies surfaced two more cases that never converged. A sealed record edited without a reseal made the rewriting repair throw an untyped TypeError (unknown_error, record_hash_mismatch:entry_1), also for _workspace. It now refuses typed with history_record_integrity_invalid, exit 4, and names the restore. The unreadable-stream remedy named pm history-repair <id>, which the decoder refuses, so it now names the salvage preview (also in validate). (4) Bulk selection: --all --append-only only when every drifted stream is a bridgeable chain mismatch or a missing stream; otherwise --all for the other repair codes, with a bridgeable mismatch keeping its per-item append-only remedy. While any stream is unreadable, unrepairable or version-skewed, every remedy stays per item, because both bulk forms would fail that row. A version-skewed stream is not previewed and keeps only its upgrade remedy, so its redundant chain_mismatch warning is dropped. The new spec tests/integration/lifecycle/history-remedies.integration.spec.ts runs every advised remedy, per item and in bulk, to a clean history_drift check.

value.text: Review round 1 on PR #1763 (Codex gpt-6.2-sol xhigh, Greptile, CodeRabbit), 2026-11-21. Fixed: (a) the reseed baseline is appended through O_APPEND to the exact bytes the under-lock check verified, or the stream is created exclusively (wx), in both repair modes. A writer that ignores the lock, or a stale-lock takeover, can therefore no longer lose bytes to a whole-file replace (appendRecordToVerifiedStream in src/sdk/history/append-only-repair.ts). The rewriting repair's own whole-file rewrite stays with pm-r5yhxn. (b) An unrepairable or version-skewed stream keeps only that verdict: its hash- and chain-mismatch warnings no longer advise a repair that refuses, and details keep the evidence. (c) A pending merge-receipt stream blocks the bulk remedies, because the bulk run would reconcile it without the merge audit. (d) A record sealed in a newer record_hash_version format now counts as version skew in the drift scan, and the rewriting repair refuses it typed with history_record_version_unsupported plus the upgrade step, instead of diagnosing corruption. (e) A reseed reports an explicit --normalize-provenance request. Declined with reason: ownership-aware health advice. Health judges the stream, not the caller's authority. Under strict ownership_enforcement the advised repair refuses typed with the --force override and still works for the assignee, and making previews enforce ownership would misclassify an owned stream as unbridgeable.

value.text: Review rounds 2 to 4 on PR #1763 (Codex gpt-6.2-sol xhigh on each new range, plus Greptile), 2026-11-21. Fixed: (a) An absent stream is published complete through createFileAtomic with sync: it stages and flushes the record beside the stream, then hard-links it into the absent path. A stream or link another writer created wins (stream_changed). A filesystem that cannot hard-link refuses typed (reason stream_publish_unsupported, AtomicLinkUnsupportedError) and writes nothing. A short-lived exclusive-open fallback was removed again, because it could interleave with writers that ignore the lock and could leave a partial baseline. Staging cleanup is best effort, so a published stream is never reported as failed. (b) A history path that is a symbolic link refuses at planning (assertRegularStreamEntry) and at apply (O_NOFOLLOW), in both modes and for the bridge. The advice is to restore the item's own stream, or to move the link aside and preview the rebuild. (c) hasNewerRecordSealFormat is one classifier shared by the drift scan and the rewriting repair. Only a complete seal in a newer numeric format is version skew with upgrade advice; a string version or an incomplete envelope is damage with restore advice. (d) A pending merge-receipt stream keeps the unrelated drift per item.

value.text: Review round 5 on PR #1763 (Codex, CodeRabbit), 2026-11-21. Changed design: the hard-link publication added in round 2 kept generating filesystem edge cases (no hard links, sync ordering, leftover staging files), so it was replaced by the bridge's own verified append path. An absent stream is created with an exclusive O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_APPEND|O_NOFOLLOW open, and the record is appended, flushed, read back and identity-checked exactly like the bridge. A stream this repair created but could not finish writing is unlinked again when it holds only this repair's bytes. createFileAtomic is unchanged from main. Fixed: the drift cache version is 13, because version_skew semantics changed for unchanged bytes. A missing stream whose history path is a link is reported as unrepairable. The no-repair code is renamed, before any release, from history_drift_chain_unrepairable to history_drift_unrepairable_stream, its remedy is the refusing preview pm history-repair <id> --dry-run, which names the recovery, and details.chain_unbridgeable is now details.repair_refusals. Salvage of a deleted item takes ownership from the last replayed state that still held the item, so strict ownership still applies.

value.text: Review round 6 on PR #1763 (Codex), 2026-11-21: design settled. The round-5 exclusive create plus unlink-on-failure was reverted, because unlink could delete a concurrent writer's bytes (P1) and an exclusive create exposes an empty stream before the baseline (P2). The absent-stream reseed is back to the round-4 publication. createFileAtomic with sync stages and flushes the record, then hard-links it into the absent path, so nothing partial or empty is ever visible. AtomicLinkUnsupportedError becomes a typed refusal (stream_publish_unsupported) that publishes nothing. Staging cleanup is best effort, so it can no longer turn a successful publication into a failure; per Codex this also fixes a false failure for mutation checkpoints on main. A test now proves the flush comes before the link. The unrepairable remedy is pm history <id> --verify --full again, because the rewriting preview's refusal is not typed for every cause (for example duplicate creates). Accepted limitation, documented in HISTORY_RECOVERY.md: on a filesystem without hard links, the preview of an absent-stream rebuild succeeds and the write refuses typed with a recovery. Probing link support during a dry run would write files.
